recipes.name: Kelly's Pressure Cooker Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
4 potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces

steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Place flour in a resealable plastic bag; add 1/2 beef cubes and shake to coat. Remove beef cubes; shake off excess flour. Add beef cubes to skillet. Repeat with remaining 1/2 beef cubes. Season beef cubes with salt and black pepper.
Stir onion into skillet; cook, stirring often, until beef cubes are browned on all sides and onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle in sugar.

Combine water, bouillon cubes, garlic, bay leaf, parsley, and basil in a pressure cooker over medium-high heat until bouillon cubes are dissolved. Place pressure cooker rack into the cooker (if it has one). Layer potatoes, carrots, and beef mixture into the pressure cooker; season with salt and black pepper. Close cooker securely and place pressure regulator over vent according to manufacturer's instructions. Bring up to full pressure until steam escapes in a steady flow and makes a whistling sound.

Reduce heat to medium-low until regulator is gently rocking, maintaining full pressure. Cook for 8 minutes. Let pressure release naturally according to manufacturer's instructions, about 15 minutes. Unlock lid and remove. Transfer beef and vegetables to a serving bowl; pour pan juices over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Kelly's Pressure Cooker Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: Kelly's pressure cooker beef stew recipe is homey and full of carrots, potatoes, and onions. It is ready in less than an hour with the pressure cooker.

review.reviewBody: Just made this tonight and was fabulous. A few changes like most cooks - omitted the sugar, added 3 stalks of celery, cut in 2 inch segments and didn't coat the meat with flour. Because I had almost double the meat, I browned the beef in divided batches, then added everything else. My 6 qt pot was pretty full so had to remove some liquid to leave the required 1/3 space at the top. ( Very important!) Also thickened mine with cornstarch. All minor changes. Very nice beef stew recipe that went from conception to table in 1 hour! Love it!

Thanks Kelly! ... With our changes to meet our tastes, this is the best beef stew I've ever enjoyed to date! [and we are in our fifties] 

We made this particular recipe tonight for supper with the following changes: 

- substituted beef broth for water and bouillon, = more hearty flavor profile and less salt
- added 1 3/4 cups of Cotes-Du-Rhone red wine into pot (moderately dry, great body, excellent with beef) it makes the broth robust and hearty in its flavor!
... - cooked onions in pot with broth, wine, 3/4" pieces of celery, garlic and herbs
- after setting aside the browned beef, added mushrooms to skillet with butter to saute' / deglaze = a better "earthy" flavor component, and great with red wine!

Of course the wine alcohol cooks out, with the wine adding to the hearty flavor profile, and leaving just a small wine flavor that only is identified as a final flavor note in each spoonful.

This recipe is now the base recipe for our future beef stews. 
Future versions will include:
- adding corn, and green beans(consider deleting celery to control liquids)etc.; for variation at times. (also are excellent versions of a beef stew)

I made this in my Instant Pot® and did all the sauteeing in that instead of on the stovetop. I also used beef stock instead of water and bouillon. After the pressure built, I realized that I completely forgot the sugar. Next time! Delicious stew in no time flat!

It worked really well in my small stovetop pressure cooker [Bella brand.] My additions maxed out the 2/3 capacity recommended. I added 8oz. quartered white mushrooms; 1c of 1/2" chopped celery; 2T of cooking sherry.

This was delicious!! I made it in the Instant Pot and it was so good! The meat was very tender and the veggies were cooked perfectly. The only thing I did was add some portabella mushrooms that we needed to use up and I thought it came out a little thin for my family's liking so I thickened the juices with flour/water. There were no leftovers and my whole family declared this is a definite repeat.
Very tasty. Will definitely make again. I also used 1 c red wine and beef broth instead of bullion and water.

This is a great recipe the only additions I made was I added dry onion soup mix and I used italian seasoning instead of basil. I also marinated my beef with worcesteshire sauce, balsamic vinegar and steak seasoning then browned with flour. Added some celery and used beef broth...YUM.

We enjoy this stew, and like most reviews I did make a few changes. I seasoned the flour with salt and pepper before dredging the meat. I don't usually have bouillon on hand so I used beef broth and also added two stalks of celery hearts. I didn't have baby carrots so I used four large carrots that I left large as we like our veggies a little crisper. I will probably make this again but would sub summer savory for the basil for a more traditional stew.
I made this recipe. I used 1 1/2 cups beef broth and 1/2 cup dry red wine instead of water and beef bullion cube. It came out delicious. my husband loved it. We had crusty bread with it.
Double the ingredients for a bigger family, and it turned out great. I did do the liquid and seasoning heating in a pot on the stove and then transferred to the preasure cooker.

I have made this several times but use less potato. This last time was a partial fail. I used a new instant pot. I went back to check and it said Burn and the lid wouldn't seal. So, I found out with the newer pots they are sensitive to liquid so the liquid in this recipe is not adequate for the newer Instant Pots. In my original LUX there was no problem.
Great flavor!
Triple the broth and added one can tomato paste
I really liked this recipe as did the rest of the family. Only thing I did different was leave the sugar out. Will be making again soon.
Wow this was delicious! Just bought a Ninja Foodi and this was my first recipe using it! I forgot the sugar but it doesn’t need it and I won’t use it in the future.

I really enjoyed the meal and came together easily. Next time I am going to add 1 table spoon of sugar; it was just a little sweet for my preference (not candy sweet). I cooked the meal at lunch time. I put the pressure cooker (electronic) at 165 warm setting until dinner time. All the flavors absorbed in to the food.

This was crazy good! I have never used basil or parsley in a stew before but was I ever pleasantly surprised. I also had never used flour to brown the meat. I think that was a key feature in the taste of this stew. Excellent and I will be making this on a regular basis. Thank you for a great recipe!
Very tasty family loved it
Fantastic recipe!
I always make changes, lol. Used some ketsup and thicker with mashed potato flakes
